verdict.rationale: Conductor documents its own cloud sandboxes where agents can test repositories and run builds, and each workspace gets an isolated worktree and running environment. Nothing in the evidence says these sandboxes are kept separate from production data or systems, so the story is only half evidenced. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that sandboxes isolate from production data/credentials, environment or data-seeding controls for test environments, and independent hands-on corroboration of sandbox isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Sandboxes spin up in seconds, and agents keep working after you close your laptop.
The agent can test your repositories, update install and setup scripts, and run builds — without asking you to confirm each step.
Create a new workspace with Command + N when work should have its own branch, files, running environment, and review path.
Conductor creates a separate working tree for each workspace. That lets agents work in parallel without editing the same files on disk.
